chunks: 9-4 My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim and Ahmad ibn Zakariya narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Na'im, from Yazid ibn Ibrahim, from one of those who narrated to him from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

By God, the Blessed and Exalted God has granted me nine things which He did not grant to anyone before me, except the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): Paths have been opened for me, I was taught the lineages, the clouds were made to flow for me, I was taught about deaths, calamities, and the distinction of speech. And I looked into the Kingdom (Malakut) by the permission of my Lord, so nothing that was before me or will come after me was hidden from me. And that through my Wilayah, God perfected for this nation their religion, completed His favor upon them, and was pleased with their Islam, as He said on the Day of Wilayah to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family): 'O Muhammad! Inform them that I have perfected for them today their religion and approved for them Islam as a religion, and I have completed My favor upon them.' All of that is from the bounty of God upon me, so to Him belongs the praise.

key_terms.الْمَلَكُوتِ: The Kingdom or Realm of Angels, referring to the unseen spiritual domain
key_terms.الْوِلَايَةِ: Wilayah, referring to the authority or guardianship of the Imam
key_terms.فَصْلَ الْخِطَابِ: The distinction or clarification of speech/judgment

ai.seo_question: What are the nine things God gave to Imam Ali that He did not give to others?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the unique spiritual and metaphysical status of Imam Ali (AS) through nine specific divine endowments, such as knowledge of lineages (*Ansab*) and calamities, which distinguish him from other prophets. It explicitly links these gifts to the perfection of Islam, reinforcing the Shia doctrine that the establishment of Wilayah was the culmination of divine revelation. The narration serves as a theological foundation for the concept of *Kamal al-Din*, asserting that religious completeness is inextricably tied to the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt.
